executiveSummary: Three incidents were open in this period and one earlier matter was closed. The significant one is the residual risk this board accepted in October: customer records sitting with our CRM vendor beyond our direct control. That acceptance fell due for re-confirmation in April and was not re-confirmed; in July the vendor was breached. It was determined material on 14 July and reported on Form 8-K on 17 July, inside the required window. A four-hour degradation of card authorisation at the EU payments subsidiary was classified as major under DORA and reported to the national competent authority, and was separately determined not material for securities purposes — two different questions with two different tests. The third, a renewed wave of credential-stuffing against the customer portal, is still under assessment and is being assessed together with the two earlier waves rather than on its own.

incidents.I-001: An earlier wave of the same credential-stuffing activity was determined not material in March and closed after credential resets and tighter rate limiting; it is retained as the reference point for the wave now under assessment.
incidents.I-002: Our CRM vendor was breached, exposing name, email, postal address and order history for 84,000 customers; payment card data is tokenised at the gateway and was not in the tenant. This is the exposure recorded as acceptance A-002 and tracked as risk R-003 — the insurance rider moved the financial loss, as anticipated, but not the notification duty or the customer-facing consequence. Determined material on 14 July on the disclosure committee's recommendation and reported on Form 8-K on 17 July, one business day inside the four-business-day window.
incidents.I-003: Card authorisation at the EU payments subsidiary ran above its service level for four hours and twelve minutes; it was classified as major under DORA, the initial notification and the intermediate report are with the national competent authority, and the final report is due by 23 August.
incidents.I-004: A third wave of credential-stuffing against the customer portal is under assessment; because it runs on the same infrastructure against the same unremediated weakness as the March and May waves, the three are being assessed as one series rather than separately, and the determination is deferred until the log review completes on 3 August.

decisions: Note the Form 8-K filed on 17 July and confirm the committee is content with the process the disclosure committee followed to reach the determination.
Re-confirm or withdraw acceptance A-002 on the record: it was due for re-confirmation in April, was not re-confirmed, and the exposure it describes has now occurred.
Fund the work that would close the weakness the three credential-stuffing waves have in common, or decide to carry it into next year with the residual risk recorded and owned.
